items.title: Infertility Training Center
Modernizing the Labor Market Test and Improving Protections for U.S. Workers in the PERM Immigrant Visa Program

data.abstract: The Department of Labor (Department or DOL) proposes to amend its regulations regarding the certification of job opportunities offered by employers seeking to employ aliens on a permanent basis in the United States. This Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM or proposed rule) strengthens the standards by which the Department receives and reviews employers' applications for permanent labor certification and improves the integrity of the overall employment-based immigrant visa program to more effectively protect the wages and job opportunities of U.S. workers similarly employed in the United States. Among the issues addressed in this proposed rule are eliminating further administration of Schedule A, which exempts certain job opportunities from the statutorily required labor market test; strengthening the minimum standards of recruitment to ensure all employers seeking labor certification access the broadest pool of high-quality U.S. workers using the latest technologies and methods; enhancing safeguards for U.S. workers impacted by layoffs, including those laid off by employers using third-party staffing companies and establishing standards for employers to report layoffs; expanding requirements for employers to provide U.S. workers with notice of filing (NOF) applications for permanent labor certification; improving employer compliance with program requirements and consideration of qualified U.S. workers that is comparable to job opportunities for which permanent labor certification is not required; and codifying the Department's practice of electronically receiving, processing, and issuing final determinations on employer requests for prevailing wages and permanent labor certifications. The changes in this proposed rule are consistent with the Secretary of Labor's (Secretary) statutory responsibilities to certify that there are not sufficient workers in the United States who are able, willing, qualified, and available to fill the petitioning employer's job opportunity at the time of application for a visa and admission to the United States, and that the employment of such alien will not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed workers in the United States.

items.title: In the Matter of TRISO-X, LLC; Confirmatory Order Modifying License

data.abstract: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is issuing a Confirmatory Order to TRISO-X, LLC (the licensee), as a result of a successful Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) mediation. On June 9, 2026, the NRC notified the licensee of an apparent violation being considered for escalated enforcement. The apparent violation involved the implementation of management measures to ensure the design basis supporting the structural stability function of the TX-1 process building's main force resisting system (MFRS) was maintained during construction. The NRC provided the licensee with the opportunity to respond through a written response, a Pre-decisional Enforcement Conference (PEC), or ADR. The licensee elected to participate in ADR, and mediation sessions were held on July 29 and August 20, 2026, during which the parties reached an Agreement in Principle. As part of the agreement, the licensee committed to taking certain corrective actions and consented to the issuance of a Confirmatory Order to make those commitments legally binding and resolve the apparent violation without further enforcement action by the NRC. The Confirmatory Order is effective upon issuance.

items.title: Chartering and Field of Membership for Federal Credit Unions; Associational Common Bonds and Client-Customer Relationships

data.abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) is issuing a final rule to amend its criteria for determining associational common bonds. The amendments clarify that requiring members to buy a good, product, or service from a group as a condition of membership will no longer automatically bar eligibility as a recognized association. After considering public comments, the Board finalizes the proposed rule with certain modifications. The Board's revisions detail how NCUA assesses client- customer relationships (including relevant examples). These changes also simplify NCUA's process for reviewing pre-approved groups.

items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Daher Aircraft, SAS

data.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2015-17-10, which applies to certain SOCATA (type certificate currently held by Daher Aircraft, SAS) (Daher) Model TBM 700 airplanes. AD 2015- 17-10 requires repetitively inspecting the forging body of the main landing gear (MLG) for cracks and, depending on findings, performing corrective actions. AD 2015-17-10 allows for replacement of affected MLG with a reinforced landing gear as a terminating action for repetitive inspections. Since the FAA issued AD 2015-17-10, additional MLG serviceable parts have been developed, and it has been determined that dye penetrant is no longer an authorized inspection method. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions of AD 2015-17-10, add the additional serviceable parts, and eliminate the option of using dye penetrant as an inspection method. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
